messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: decode_latency_p99 > 2.0s in cluster us-west-2 for 6m. Streaming stall errors rising. Impacting hosted inference routes /v1/stream and /v1/generate. Auto-sla-breach:true. alert_id=INC-2026-314-KERNEL-REG

alex wang: oncall here, I'm taking this. adding @maria gomez and @ryan choi. quick ask: is this correlated with any recent kernel/compiler rollout?

maria gomez: yes, we rolled trt kernel `trt-v2.3-flashattn` to canary at 2026-03-14T02:00 UTC and started ramp at 02:35 -> 50% traffic by 03:10. also landed a compile flag change `-O3 -floop-strip-mine` in the decode compiler.

ryan choi: build infra confirmed the compiler flag was toggled in the nightly build at 2026-03-14T01:58 UTC and the kernel package `trt-v2.3-flashattn` was published at 02:04.

alex wang: ok. can someone check p95/p99 and streaming stall traces for the affected nodes? priority: mitigate live.

maria gomez: pulling metrics now: baseline p95 decode ~ 120ms, p99 ~ 420ms. After ramp p95 -> 360ms, p99 -> 2.8s. Streaming stalls (frame drops) up 8x. logs show repeated `kv_cache_miss` + `cuda_sync_timeout` on decode path.

kai tanaka: my hunch: new flashattn kernel plus aggressive compiler flag interacts with long-seq decode hot paths, causing paging-like stalls when KV cache spans >12MB per request. Could be memory access pattern changed leading to device page thrash.

alex wang: plan: 1) remove new kernel from runtime routing 2) revert compiler flag for the next rolling deploy 3) enable fallback model variant (quantized) for heavy customers. Who can run the kernel revert?

maria gomez: I can flip runtime routing. Doing safe rollback to `trt-v2.2` on a small subset first. command:```bash
# runtime routing rollback
rctl runtime set-kernel --cluster=us-west-2 --pool=decode --kernel=trt-v2.2 --wait
# or k8s fallback
kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/decoder-runtime KERNEL_VERSION=trt-v2.2
```

ryan choi: I'll prepare a hotfix build with the compiler flag reverted and push to canary tag `decode-hotfix-20260314`. build will include a regression test.

sre-bot: automated check: rolling update started for deployment/decoder-runtime (us-west-2) at 1845679065. health checks enabled.

maria gomez: rolled back kernel routing to `trt-v2.2` on 20% of decode pool @ 03:05 UTC. p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 780ms on those nodes. continuing rollout to 100%.

jamal barker: customer success: informed top impacted customers (acme-inc, dataflow-app) about temporary mitigation (fallback to quantized variant). acme reported noticeable improvement after fallback.

alex wang: nice. ryan how long for compiler-flag revert build? can we cut a canary and measure with the long-seq streaming test?

ryan choi: ETA ~18m for canary artifact + 10m for canary rollout. I'll attach the reproduce command for local devs:
```bash
python bench/decode_latency.py --model redwood-open-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --kernel trt-v2.3 --iters 200
# compare against trt-v2.2 and with/without -floop-strip-mine
```

maria gomez: after full rollback of kernel routing at 03:18 UTC cluster p95 ~ 210ms, p99 ~ 560ms. still above baseline but well under SLO breach threshold. continuing to monitor.

sre-bot: automated alert: SLO breach cleared at 1845679260.

ryan choi: pushed `decode-hotfix-20260314` canary at 03:28 UTC with compiler flags reverted. running long-seq synthetic. initial canary p99 ~ 520ms, looks stable.

kai tanaka: we should still bisect flags + kernel patches offline. action: reproduce, run mem-access profiler, run flashattn microbench across long prefix sizes.

alex wang: agreed. short-term mitigation complete: kernel rollback + compile-flag revert. Customer impact: transient p99 spikes for ~40m affecting streaming clients; no data loss, increased tail latency and stalls causing some client reconnects. Customer comms queued by @jamal barker.

jamal barker: customers notified, incident triage note shared with accounts. one customer requested an RCA and timeline.

maria gomez: next steps for eng-runtime: 1) bisect trt-v2.3 patches 2) add long-seq decode regression to CI (seq>=2048, KV cache pressure) 3) add runtime guard to avoid routing trt-v2.3 to nodes with >12GB active KV cache 4) add metric for `kv_cache_evictions/sec` to alert earlier.

alex wang: handing back to oncall rotation. please create postmortem with timeline and link to this thread. tag: eng-runtime, eng-ml, eng-infra. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident INC-2026-314-KERNEL-REG marked resolved at 1845679480.

alex wang: thanks everyone — great quick coordination. I'll own the follow-ups with maria and ryan for the postmortem.
